To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
user-deployed networks can provide a good service perception, especially if the users are able to cooperate through a peer-to- peer exchange".

(1) the user service perception is acceptable in user-deployed infrastructures with a low density of APs; (2) the user service experience can be further improved by introducing a peer-to-peer content exchange between terminals, and (3) this can be done without the need to increase the number of APs, or to increase the bandwidth available to the terminals.

(i) the user-deployed infrastructure can be exploited for delivering "infotainment"-type services, (ii) peer-to-peer cooperation can significantly reduce the infrastructure requirements and/or improve the service perception.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the service provisioning capabilities in user-deployed wireless networks.

the investigation of the impact of user-deployed APs on the provision of "infotainment", and with the evaluation of the potential benefits deriving from the adoption of peer-to-peer strategies for information pre-fetching.
the investigation of the service perception in spotty networks and the impact of peer cooperation on the infrastructure requirements and service perception.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
user-deployed infrastructures can be a viable solution for future radio access networks, especially when used in combination with a peer-to-peer cooperation strategy.
user-deployed APs, when properly exploited through peer-to-peer cooperation, are a very promising solution for providing infotainment services in public infrastructures.

the proposed framework is able to provide the user service perception for a variety of different services, and that the proposed opportunistic peer-to-peer cooperation strategy is able to significantly reduce infrastructure requirements and improve service perception.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in user-deployed infrastructures, the adoption of an opportunistic peer-to-peer content exchange strategy, can bring significant gains in terms of infrastructure requirements and service perception.

, even in a spotty network environment, it is possible to deliver acceptable service perception for non-interactive services, and that the use of peer-to-peer file sharing can bring substantial infrastructure and service gains.

the proposed framework is able to provide a quantitative evaluation of the impact of infrastructure and terminal cooperation on the user service perception, and thus, to support the decision process of the network operator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the user-deployed APs, even when deployed without any coordination, can deliver acceptable user service perception, especially if the services are not too time critical.
, even in spotty coverage networks, the user service perception can be improved by means of opportunistic terminal cooperation.
, with appropriate cooperation, a user-deployed infrastructure can provide satisfactory services to its end users.
